title: How a solid catalyst works
caption: Hydrogenating ethene on nickel: the gases adsorb onto the metal surface, which weakens their bonds; they react on the surface; the product desorbs, freeing the site. Adsorption must be strong enough to weaken bonds but weak enough to let the product go.
alt: A cycle: free Ni surface → H₂ and C₂H₄ adsorbed → reaction on the surface → ethane desorbs → free surface.
description: Adsorption: H₂ and C₂H₄ bond to the nickel surface.
Reaction: hydrogen atoms add to the adsorbed ethene.
Desorption: ethane leaves, freeing the surface for the next molecules.
